headline: Kai, the first rate hike in three years is on the books, the 10-year sits at 5 percent, and the market's verdict was a shrug.
subline: Warsh signals one more hike this year, Brent eases to $103.87 as Aramco reroutes around its damaged pipeline, and bitcoin is back above $80,000.
asof: Weekend edition · as of ~6:40 AM ET Saturday, Sep 19 · stocks, yields and commodities are Friday's close; bitcoin is live · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Stocks close out hike week without damage
items.sentence: The S&P 500 added 0.17 percent Friday to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq 0.39 percent to 26,522.55, while the 10-year yield finished the Fed's hike week at 5.00 percent, up 5.3 basis points, per TheStreet.

items.title: Warsh's Fed pencils in one more hike
items.sentence: Wednesday's quarter-point move to 3.75–4.00 percent came with August inflation at 3.4 percent, and projections show one more increase this year and none in 2027, per NPR.

items.title: Brent slips to $103.87 as Aramco reroutes
items.sentence: Brent fell 0.91 percent Friday and 1.2 percent on the week as Saudi Arabia pushed 2.8 million barrels a day through Hormuz — versus 700,000 in August — and Aramco signaled half the damaged pipeline's flows will return, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Bitcoin reclaims $80,000 as hike nerves fade
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades at $81,247.25 early Saturday, up 3.88 percent in 24 hours on more than $180 million in short liquidations — a sharp rebound off the sub-$78,000 levels that followed the Fed's hike, per CoinDesk.

items.title: Next week: flash PMIs, Costco, $192B in auctions
items.sentence: S&P Global flash PMIs land Wednesday, new home sales and Costco's report come Thursday, durable goods and final Michigan sentiment close the week, and the Treasury sells $78B in 2-year, $70B in 5-year and $44B in 7-year notes, per Investrade's calendar.

items.title: Iran fire pause reaches nine days
items.sentence: Tehran has held its fire for nine straight days and the coalition has gone eleven without strikes on Iranian territory, the quietest stretch since spring, per GlobalSecurity's day-203 report.

items.title: CBO calls the war inflation's main engine
items.sentence: A Congressional Budget Office report identified the Iran conflict as the primary driver of the inflation still working through American households, per NPR's weekly roundup.

items.title: Houthis tighten grip on Bab el-Mandeb
items.sentence: After seizing the port of Mokha, Houthi forces captured more Red Sea islands commanding the strait that carries much of the world's seaborne trade, per Euronews.

items.title: Supreme Court blocks mail-ballot order
items.sentence: The justices declined to let the administration enforce its executive order restricting mail-in voting ahead of the midterms, per Votebeat.

items.title: US approves $2.8 billion arms package for Israel
items.sentence: The package features 2,000-pound bombs in the largest recent sale of that munition, per NPR's weekly roundup.

items.title: Frontier labs sketch a private AI watchdog
items.sentence: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google have spent weeks discussing a standards body that would screen the most advanced models and coordinate slowdowns if dangers emerge — over open White House skepticism, per TechCrunch.

items.title: Unredacted filings sharpen the Times's case
items.sentence: A Microsoft director privately called AI data scraping 'the largest theft of labor in human history,' and Microsoft's own data showed Copilot answers cutting click-throughs to the Times by up to 93 percent, per TechCrunch.

items.title: SEC opens a lane for tokenized stocks
items.sentence: Thursday's 'Innovation Exemption' creates a regulated path for trading tokenized versions of US-listed stocks, per the SEC, and Coinbase and Robinhood rose 6.55 and 5.94 percent Friday on the news, per TheStreet.

items.title: Claude now does a quarter of Anthropic's R&D
items.sentence: Anthropic says Claude completed roughly 26 percent of its research and engineering work by August — up from about zero in February — with some 30,000 agents on the job, per TechStartups' roundup.

items.title: Huang sees Nvidia chip sales doubling in 2027
items.sentence: Fresh off a $96.2 billion quarter that grew 106 percent year over year, Nvidia's CEO projects the company will sell twice as many chips in 2027 as in 2026, per TechStartups' roundup.
